messages:
Mike: ran cross-region slice + prefill/decode sweep this morning, posting quick summary. used GPU-slicing on A100 (40G slices) vs native H100 nodes.
Anya: nice, did you keep batch size and sequence lengths consistent?
Mike: yup — prefill 128 tokens, decode 512, batch=1/4/8 microbatches. same tokenizer, same prompt set (2000 prompts).
Raj: curious about quantization. int8 vs int4? any QoR diffs?
Mike: ran int8 and q4 with GPTQ-style calibrate. quality delta tracked with eval set — small BLEU/ROUGE drop for q4 on Mistral-7B (~0.8% BLEU), decode artifacts on a few long prompts.
Lena: can you paste the numbers? rough latency + tokens/sec + cost per 1M tokens.
Mike: sure — TL;DR numbers (prefill latency / decode latency / tokens/sec / $/1M tokens):
```
Model          | A100-40G-slice (int8)   | H100 (int8)
---------------------------------------------------------
Llama2-7B      | prefill 28ms / decode 115ms  | prefill 21ms / decode 82ms
               | 750 tps                    | 1020 tps
               | $11.8 / 1M tokens          | $9.4 / 1M tokens
Mistral-7B     | prefill 31ms / decode 132ms | prefill 23ms / decode 95ms
               | 680 tps                    | 920 tps
               | $12.9 / 1M tokens          | $10.2 / 1M tokens
Falcon-7B      | prefill 26ms / decode 120ms | prefill 20ms / decode 88ms
               | 720 tps                    | 980 tps
               | $12.0 / 1M tokens          | $9.6 / 1M tokens
```
Notes: A100 used 40GB slicing (2 slices per GPU) which hurts decode kernel peak but improves amortized cost in high-util patterns. H100 delivered lower latency and better tokens/sec despite higher per-hour price — overall $/1M still lower for H100 because of throughput gains.
Anya: thanks. how did kernels fall through? triton autotune vs our bespoke kernels?
Mike: we used runtime kernel selection: default to cuBLAS/FlashAttention2 on H100, fallback to older flash kernels for some shapes on A100-slice. For Mistral we saw a kernel mismatch at decode length 512 that forced a slower path on A100 slices.
perf-bot: automated-run:2160001100 completed. 2000 prompts, 3 repeats. artifacts logged to s3://redwood-perf/gpu-slice/2160001111/
Raj: region-wise differences? you mentioned cross-region.
Mike: ran us-east1 and europe-west1. latencies + egress differences: H100 in eu-west slightly higher decode tail (+6-8ms) vs us-east, tokens/sec similar. cost delta due to region price: eu ~ +8% on $/1M.
Lena: any regressions that would block rolling this quantization config to prod?
Mike: short answer: for Llama2-7B and Falcon-7B int8 looks safe. Mistral q4 shows small quality regressions on a small set of prompts — recommend canary in Dedicated for a few customers, keep fallback to unquantized model for flagged routes.
Anya: can we tune kernel selection to avoid the A100 decode fallthrough? maybe tweak sequence slicing or prefill chunking?
Mike: yes — two knobs helped: (1) increase prefill chunk to align with native kernel tiling (prefill->256 for some batches) and (2) avoid 40G 2-slice packing when decode-heavy — use single-slice at slightly higher cost but avoid slow kernel. I have a quick script to decide slice packing by workload.
Raj: paste command used so I can reproduce locally.
Mike: here's the run command:
```
./run_infer_bench --model {model} --region {us-east1|eu-west1} --gpu {a100|h100} --slice 40G|native --quant int8|q4 --prefill 128 --decode 512 --repeats 3 --out s3://redwood-perf/gpu-slice/2160001111/
```
Lena: pinging infra to add a small H100 canary pool for dedicated customers if we decide to move forward. @Anya can you draft rollout notes?
Anya: on it. will include fallback policy, per-route pin, and eval thresholds.
Mike: also noting ops: if we enable auto-routing to H100 for latency-sensitive routes, add cost cap triggers — fallback to A100 when price/throughput delta exceeds thresholds.
perf-bot: note: recorded kernel mismatch events: 43 on a100-slice runs, 2 on h100. logs: s3://redwood-perf/logs/2160001111/kernels.json
Raj: thanks — i'll try reproduce the kernel miss on an A100 slice in my rack tomorrow.
Lena: great thread. if no objections i’ll start a tiny canary next week and surface results in eng-ml. :thumbsup:
Mike: perfect. attaching eval diff CSV in the bucket. will follow up with a short PR to our serving defaults (kernel hints + slice heuristics).
